input_basis: general knowledge and independent authorial possibilities; no project-local data
authorial_exploration_region: fictional place and person with unusual time or spatial scale, agent-owned only

possibilities.setting: a vast subterranean soil conservatory in a repurposed quarry
possibilities.cause: a cracked irrigation pipe sends water into a rooted soil bed
possibilities.response: a keeper fits a small diversion ridge of cohesive clay so runoff flows away from exposed roots
possibilities.consequence: water turns around the clay ridge, leaving a shallow silt fan downstream while dark crumbly soil stays on the roots

possibilities.setting: a huge unfinished earthen temple terrace
possibilities.cause: overnight water cuts a rill toward the nursery
possibilities.response: a worker presses a clay barrier into the rill
possibilities.consequence: the runoff bends away from a surviving sapling and deposits a pale sediment fan

possibilities.era: a future generation ship nearing its first sunrise at destination
possibilities.setting: the working end of a long cylindrical soil nursery
possibilities.cause: condensation discharge has washed a furrow through the bed
possibilities.response: a cultivator seals the shortcut with cohesive earth and presses loose loam back against a rootball
possibilities.consequence: runoff follows the restored channel; damaged and repaired material remain visibly distinct

possibilities.era: the final morning before a fictional ancient reservoir is refilled
possibilities.setting: an immense dry reservoir with earthen terraces
possibilities.cause: a sluice leak starts to wet the cracked basin floor
possibilities.response: a woman lifts a root-bound block of living soil into a low tray
possibilities.consequence: the rescued root ball retains dark soil while surrounding pale earth fractures into large dry plates

possibilities.era: late nineteenth century in a fictional abandoned earth amphitheatre
possibilities.setting: a giant clay-cut amphitheatre facing a low sun
possibilities.cause: seasonal rain has reopened a runoff scar on the lowest steps
possibilities.response: a restorer packs cohesive damp clay into the scar
possibilities.consequence: hand presses and a fresh smooth patch contrast with coarse old rammed earth

possibilities.era: a near-future vineyard after a prolonged drought
possibilities.setting: narrow living terraces inside a vast disused quarry
possibilities.cause: the first irrigation stream loosens the retaining berm
possibilities.response: a keeper consolidates moist loam around a exposed vine root
possibilities.consequence: the restored berm redirects water and shows finger presses alongside distinct crumbled soil
